You're auditing the Nxeon v2 customer portal (Next.js app) at /opt/nxeon-v2, running locally at http://localhost:3021 (NXEON_SANDBOX=1 — Proxmox provisioning, Stripe card charges, and DB Studio's live SQL are stubbed; everything else is real, hitting a real Postgres DB). This is close to a production promotion, so find REAL bugs via REAL hands-on Playwright testing, not a code read. Any throwaway Playwright scripts must live inside /opt/nxeon-v2 (module resolution requires it) — delete them when done.

Login: admin@nxeon.local / iCwEt7PDdo0ne3YM (has ~14 existing services of various kinds: VPS, game servers, shared hosting, business email — good for this audit since you need real data to look at).

YOUR SCOPE: /dashboard (the main dashboard home) and /dashboard/services (My Services) including drilling into individual service detail/management pages (VPS server management, game server management, hosting account management — click "Manage" on a few different service types and explore what opens).

WHAT TO ACTUALLY DO:
1. On /dashboard: check the stats tiles, the services table/list, the resource-usage donuts, the "Deploy New Service" quick-tile row (verify displayed prices look real, not $0.00 or obviously wrong — a past bug had Business Email showing $0.00 due to a bad DB query), the promo carousel on the right rail (click through EVERY slide's CTA button and confirm it navigates somewhere real — a past bug had these as inert buttons with no onClick at all), and the recent-activity feed.
2. On /dashboard/services: test each tab filter (All/VPS/Game Servers/Shared Hosting/Free Services), the search box, sort dropdown, status/location filters. Open a few individual services via "Manage" and check their management pages load real data and their action buttons (restart, reinstall, backup, etc. — whatever's available) at least render correctly, even if you don't actually trigger a destructive sandboxed action. For a shared-hosting service specifically, check its card's preview image — it should show either the customer's own captured site thumbnail (if one exists) or a stock plate / live site iframe, never a broken image or an awkward white box with a small icon floating in the corner.
3. CRITICAL — test in BOTH dark mode and light mode (toggle via topbar button, or set localStorage nx-theme=light before load via page.addInitScript for the more realistic returning-user path). Check the My Services hero banner specifically at both a normal (1600px) and a very wide (1900-2000px) browser width — there's a decorative rack image there that has previously overlapped a "SAME INFRASTRUCTURE / A BRIGHTER TOMORROW" tagline text at wide viewports.
4. Check the browser console for errors/React hydration warnings on every page load.
5. Check the sidebar navigation itself for any rendering artifacts — a past bug had a thin 1px bright line down the sidebar's right edge in light mode, from the scrollable nav list's internal overflow.

Report back with concrete, specific findings only (component/file names if identifiable, exact repro steps, screenshot paths under /tmp if saved). If something genuinely works, say so — don't invent findings. Do NOT fix anything yourself, this is discovery only.

content.content: # Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server — mistakes here are not sandboxed.** The `db` subcommand refusing obvious writes is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary; the access itself is full root. **Update, 2026-09-12: the owner authorized this session to build, deploy, and promote the Nexion portal to production directly from here** — including running `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` and `scripts/promote-production.sh` on node-1, and writing to the prod DB as those scripts require (`prisma db push --accept-data-loss` on the way to production is the expected, sanctioned behavior of that script, not a mistake to avoid). ## Audit Report: /dashboard and /dashboard/services

Tested hands-on with Playwright (Chromium) against the running app at `localhost:3021`, logged in as `admin@nxeon.local`, across dark/light mode and multiple viewport widths (1440–2200px). All scratch scripts lived under `/opt/nxeon-v2/.audit-tmp` and have been deleted.

### Confirmed bugs

**1. Dashboard home undercounts services — excludes Shared Hosting and Free Services entirely**
- `/dashboard`'s "Total Services" stat tile shows **11**, and its services-widget tabs show VPS 8 / Game Servers 3 / **Shared Hosting 0**.
- `/dashboard/services` (the real, correct data) shows **14** total: VPS 8 / Game Servers 3 / **Shared Hosting 2** / Free Services 1.
- Root cause: `app/dashboard/page.tsx` builds its `servers`/`rows`/`stats` exclusively from `db.server.findMany(...)` (lines ~79, 166-223), while the correct `/dashboard/services` page uses `lib/nx/services.ts`'s `listServices()`, which also pulls hosting accounts and free services. The dashboard's headline stat and per-type tab counts silently drop two whole service categories — the same class of bug as the historical "$0.00 Business Email" bad-query issue, just on the main dashboard.

**2. VPS/Game Server "Manage" pages: metrics permanently broken + perpetual console errors**
- Every server detail page (both VPS and Game Server types, e.g. `/dashboard/servers/<id>`) shows a permanent "Couldn't read the hypervisor" / "Metrics are temporarily unavailable — the hypervisor may be busy" banner, plus a Server Health panel stuck at "2/6 checked" with CPU/Memory/Disk/Hypervisor "Not reported".
- Confirmed via DB query: **all 17 servers in this environment have `vmid: null`** (expected in sandbox, since Proxmox provisioning is stubbed).
- Root cause: `app/api/metrics/route.ts` (line 23) and `app/api/servers/[id]/disk/route.ts` (line 42) both do `if (!server || ... || !server.vmid) return 404`. A missing `vmid` is treated identically to "not found/not yours," instead of going through the same route's own graceful fallback (`{ data: [], unavailable: true }`, HTTP 200) that already exists for a real Proxmox-connection failure. Result: the client polls these endpoints every 30s/60s forever and gets a 404 every time — confirmed via network trace (`/api/metrics?serverId=...&tf=hour` and `/api/servers/<id>/disk?tf=day` both 404), which also means the copy ("Nothing is wrong with your server — this fills in on the next refresh") is actively false — it never fills in. This isn't purely a sandbox artifact either: in production a server between "provisioning job queued" and "vmid assigned" would hit the exact same permanently-misleading state.
- Affects: `components/customer/gamepanel` (game server overview) and the VPS server overview tab identically. Shared Hosting and Business Email management pages were unaffected (they don't hit these endpoints).

**3. My Services hero: tagline text overlaps the rack artwork**
- On `app/dashboard/services/page.tsx`, the right-aligned "SAME INFRASTRUCTURE. / A BRIGHTER / TOMORROW." tagline overlaps the decorative rack image's rightmost server tower (letters render directly across the rack chassis/LED graphic).
- Verified this is **not just a "very wide" viewport issue** — pixel-level crops confirmed the overlap is present identically at 1600px (the "normal" baseline) and at 1920/2000px, because the header's geometry (rack box fixed at 440px wide, tagline fixed ~199px wide, ~233px gap between them) is essentially constant once the header is wide enough, and the `max-w-[1520px]` wrapper caps out around ~1730px viewport anyway, making 1600–2200px render nearly pixel-identical.
- The code's own comment (`app/dashboard/services/page.tsx` lines 37-48) documents an earlier attempt to fix exactly this overlap by narrowing/fading the mask sooner — that fix is insufficient: the tagline's left edge still lands inside the mask's fully-opaque region (45–68% of the box), so real bright pixels of the source photo render behind the text.

**4. VPS and Game Server detail pages ignore light mode**
- Setting `nx-theme=light` (or toggling via the topbar) correctly re-skins `/dashboard`, `/dashboard/services`, shared-hosting management, and business-email management to a white/light theme.
- On VPS (`/dashboard/servers/<id>`) and Game Server detail pages, only the topbar changes (sun icon, lighter topbar background) — the entire content area (hero card, tabs, resource panels, Players Online, Quick Actions, Server Health) stays fully dark-themed, identical pixel-for-pixel to dark mode. This is scoped specifically to these two detail-page templates; every other page tested reskins correctly.

### Verified working (no issues found)
- Dashboard quick-tile prices are all real and non-zero: VPS $8.88/mo, Game Servers $2.99/mo, Cloud Hosting $2.99/mo, Business Email $1.99/mo — the historical "$0.00 Business Email" bug does not reproduce.
- Promo carousel: all 6 slides' dots and CTAs work correctly, including the external Discord link opening a real new tab (`https://discord.com/invite/hqVZdDJH2`) with `target=_blank`/`rel=noopener`. (Note: my first several test attempts falsely suggested broken clicks — that was purely a Playwright timing artifact from the carousel's own 3.6s autoplay racing against multi-step scripted interactions; hovering — which the component correctly uses to pause autoplay — resolves it, confirmed consistently across repeated runs.)
- Sidebar in light mode: no bright 1px hairline on the scrollable nav's right edge — the fix is already in place (`components/nx/Shell.tsx` line 110, `overflow-x-hidden` alongside `overflow-y-auto`, with a comment describing the exact historical bug). Note `components/portal/Shell.tsx` still lacks this fix, but that component isn't the one rendered for `/dashboard` (dead import in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`), so it's not currently reachable.
- My Services tabs (All/VPS/Game/Shared Hosting/Free), search box (including empty-state "No services match those filters"), status filter, location filter, and sort dropdown (verified "Highest Cost" produces genuinely descending prices, "Name (A-Z)" produces alphabetical order) all work correctly with no console errors.
- Shared-hosting service cards show a proper stock "rack" placeholder graphic labeled "Placeholder" — never a broken image or an awkward white box.
- Business Email, Shared Hosting management pages load real data (mailbox counts, domain, storage, renewal dates) cleanly with no console errors.
- No React hydration warnings observed on any page load.

### Environment note
Partway through testing, another session on this same box (`nxeon-fsn1`) ran `rebuild.sh` twice, briefly taking `nxeon-v2-web` down (~90s each time) while it rebuilt/restarted; I waited rather than interfering, per this being someone else's operation on a shared box.
